day. These episodes sometimes include left arm. The pain is 
always in the setting of worsening voice hoarseness. Pain is 
always ___ and has not increased in severity or frequency since 
it started a few months ago. No pain for past several days.  
She has been experiencing dyspnea on exertion for months as 
well. Patient also notices a ""tightness"" in her chest when she 
lies down which feels different than her reflux. Patient 
recently saw ___ who peformed CT chest which was neg.
  
Patient's PCP checked troponin and called patient to come into

___.

negative. Last was a few years ago at ___. At ___, 
last was ___ which was neg exercise MIBI. Never had cath. 
 
Patient's hoarseness is new over past few months. No longer 
smoking, but has 10 pack/yr hx. Was planning to see ENT on 
___ for eval. Patient has been fatigued for years, but notes 
it is worse over past few months. Has been sent home from work 
for past month. Denies any weight loss, fever or chills. Of 
note, she has mild intermittent swelling in lower extremities at 
baseline. Also has hx of bulimia in her early ___, but denies 
any since. Reports feeling down, but denies SI.  

Patient experienced shortness of breath as she walked from 
garage to the ED. In ED, patient was chest pain free and did not 
have shortness of breath.

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted for elevated cardiac enzymes in the 
setting of a few months of stable intermittent chest pain.  The 
patient had reported chest pain approx twice per day that is 
often accompanied by voice hoarseness. During this hospital 
stay, the patient has been asymptomatic for the duration of the 
stay with no CP/Palps/SOB or PND or orthopnea.  Her troponin 
remained flat at 0.04  and her CKMB decreased from ___.  
Notably she presented with a Creatinine of 2.6 which improved to 
2.2 on day 2 of her stay. At this time it is thought that her 
___ plus recently elevated CK to 215 may have contributed to her 
positive cardiac enzymes. We noted that the patient was taking 
atorvastatin 80 mg and reduced this to 40 mg. In the setting of 
her long standing Diabetes and DOE it is certainly possible the 
patient has some CAD, however at this time it is believed her 
symptoms are related to her GERD/hoarseness.  We believe she is 
stable for outpatient follow up by her PCP, ENT and with Stress 
Echo ___.  

Transitional Issues

function and MB elevation may be due to statin-diltiazem 
interaction.
- Recommend outpatient follow up for medication adjustment

interaction and using other adjunctive HTN medications such as 
amlodipine
-Hoarseness with Chest pain. Continue to follow up with ENT

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms ___, 

You were admitted to the hospital with elevated cardiac blood 
tests (Troponin 0.04 and CK MB of 15) in the setting of stable 
intermittent chest pain which has been ongoing for months.  In 
the hosptial your cardiac blood tests were stable or decreased 
and you had no changes on your EKG. Your kidney function was 
slightly worse than normal (Creatinine 2.6) which was most 
likely the cause of your elevated cardiac markers, but improved 
during your stay (Creatinine 2.2).  You had no episodes of chest 
pain or SOB while in the hospital.  At this point you were 
deemed stable for follow up outpatient with ENT, your PCP and 
with ___ Cardiac Stress Echo in ___. It was felt that some of 
your muscle enzyme markers were elevated because of the 
interaction between your diltiazem and atorvastatin.  Thus, the 
atorvastatin dose was decreased.
